A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoG research. All 29 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including Appendices A–E, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original downstream prediction experiments, oracle comparisons and ablation studies in Tables 2–8 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original downstream prediction experiments, ablations, backbone evaluations and generated-schema case studies in Tables 2–6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: V2 adds DeepJoin similarity scores to the generation context, introduces self-reflection, and replaces the single-action prompt with batched action outputs. Section 4.3 also specifies averaging four GNNs for oracle scoring. These revise generation and selection procedures. Column unfolding already appeared in v1's appendix prompt and is not a new component.

E1.justification: The eight datasets, 12 evaluated prediction tasks and synthetic/anonymous MAG tests remain. V2 specifies AutoG inputs without supplied key relationships and with inferred column types (Sections 2.1, 4.1 and 5.1); v1 centers partially linked schemas and discusses metadata-free input as an extension. This revises the input scenario within retained application coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparator families remain. However, the IEEE-CIS expert comparator changes from region/country relations to MatchStatus, product, card and email relations (Figure 6 in both versions). The consolidated appendix comparison also ceases separately reporting both Row2Node and Row2Node/Edge variants for RGAT. HGT and PNA were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an explicit control renaming identical columns to prevent name-matching shortcuts (Section 5.2). Its LLM-backbone trials also change, including Llama 3.1 70B and Mistral 2 in Appendix E.2. The downstream GNN set and task metrics remain; omitted hyperparameter documentation does not establish changed tuning.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 adds extensive AutoG-versus-expert schema case analyses, including missing RetailRocket relations and task-specific MAG outputs. V2 replaces the quantitative LLM-backbone study with qualitative findings and removes the detailed alternative-oracle exploration and code-generation error example. The prompt-component and anonymous-MAG ablation is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Repeated candidate generation remains a search procedure rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark and ablation entries change. In Table 3, AutoG's RetailRocket AUC changes from 82.53 to 74.78, Movielens from 66.54 to 69.10, and IEEE-CIS from 90.36 to 89.17. Appendix backbone scores and generated-schema findings also change substantially. These results must be interpreted under the revised method, input conditions and expert comparator.

T1.justification: The formal definitions of tabular data, column types and heterogeneous graphs remain unchanged. Neither version develops theorems or proofs; the expanded normalization and network-effect discussions are conceptual explanations.

C1.justification: V2 removes the introduction's precise claim of achieving 98.5% of expert performance on nine tasks and describes AutoG as a preliminary solution for moderately complex scenarios in the conclusion. The central contributions—a graph-construction benchmark and an LLM-based solution approaching expert quality—remain.

C2.justification: IEEE-CIS changes from an example of successful semantic augmentation to a failure case showing that plausible normalization need not benefit prediction. V2 develops network-effect limitations and emphasizes deciding whether graphs help, whether useful graphs can be constructed, and which relations should be pruned. The existing MAG homophily explanation and dependence on column semantics remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds project-specific code-access information, a full type-inference prompt, action-function documentation and expanded generation examples. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit learning-rate, hidden-size and dropout search ranges, detailed oracle implementation discussion, and several dataset provenance/preprocessing instructions. Reproducibility documentation therefore changes substantially in both directions.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the GAN-inspired framing with a data-science-pipeline reference and introduces NetEffect-based positioning, LLM graph-reasoning work and additional model citations. NetInfoF and naming-expansion references are removed. Section 6 and Appendix C otherwise retain substantially the same research landscape.

P1.justification: Sections 4–5, the conclusion and Appendices D–E undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization. AutoG variants are renamed, the LLM discussion moves into the appendix, prompt documentation is restructured, and acknowledgments replace the reproducibility statement. These changes extend well beyond local language corrections.

P2.justification: Many original-input schema diagrams are replaced with AutoG-output diagrams, with additional AVS and task-specific MAG comparisons. V1's separate RGAT and HGT/PNA tables are consolidated, while the quantitative LLM table disappears. Figure 1's annotations and numerous figure placements, captions and table structures also change.

improvement.justification: V2 provides more informative generated-schema examples, a useful IEEE-CIS failure analysis, expanded prompts and project-specific code-access information. However, it removes explicit tuning ranges and quantitative LLM evidence while revising the expert comparator and many scores. These material gains and losses leave the overall quality direction uncertain.
